title: Six-instruction assembler and virtual machine
instructions:
Implement a tiny assembly language and its VM in two interacting modules.

## Files
- `assembler.py`: `assemble(source: str) -> list[tuple]`.
- `vm.py`: `run(source: str, max_steps: int = 100) -> dict`, calling assemble.

The source is a string. Strip each line's `#` comment and outer whitespace;
ignore blank lines. Tokens are separated by whitespace, with no commas.
A line can begin with one label `name:` optionally followed by an instruction
(whitespace after the colon is optional). Labels match ASCII
`[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, are case sensitive and unique, and point to the next
instruction's zero-based index. Labels at the end may point one past the last
instruction. Forward references are allowed. No more than one label per line.

Exactly six uppercase instructions exist:
- `SET r n`: set register r to signed decimal integer n.
- `ADD r n`: add signed decimal integer n to register r.
- `JMP label`: jump unconditionally.
- `JNZ r label`: jump when register r is nonzero, otherwise advance.
- `OUT r`: append register r's current integer value to output.
- `HALT`: stop execution.

Registers are exactly lowercase a, b, c, d. Integers match `[+-]?[0-9]+`
(no exponent or underscores). Unknown opcodes/registers/labels, duplicate or
invalid labels, invalid integers, and wrong operand counts raise ValueError.
Error message text is unspecified. `assemble` returns tuples with resolved
integer targets, e.g. [('SET', 'a', 2), ('JNZ', 'a', 0), ('HALT',)]. It must
validate the whole source, including unreachable instructions.

`run` initializes all four registers to zero on every call. Execution starts
at instruction zero; ordinary instructions advance by one. Integers have
Python's unbounded arithmetic. Return exactly {'registers': {'a': int, 'b':
int, 'c': int, 'd': int}, 'output': list[int], 'steps': int, 'halted': bool}.
Every executed instruction, including HALT and jumps, counts as one step.
`halted` is true only for an executed
HALT, false when execution falls off the end (including jumps to an end
label and empty programs). Registers/output are independent across calls.

max_steps must be a positive integer excluding bool, otherwise ValueError.
Raise RuntimeError if another instruction would execute after max_steps
instructions have executed. Reaching HALT or the end on exactly max_steps
is successful. Source syntax errors propagate as ValueError even if they
occur after an unreachable HALT. Use no eval or exec.
